title: Wear-leveling-inspired stripe allocator and eviction playbook
content:
Summary:
This note proposes a compact, low-overhead allocator and eviction strategy for the KV cache that borrows ideas from flash wear-leveling and stripe-based allocation. The goal is to reduce fragmentation, distribute write/amend pressure across arenas, and improve multi-tenant fairness without heavy global compaction pauses.

Motivation / Problem statement:
- We observe small-object churn concentrated on a subset of cache slots creating hot "islands" that force frequent local compaction while leaving other arenas underutilized.
- Aggressive per-tenant quotas can lead to cross-tenant unfairness when placements are naive (first-fit or LRU-only).
- Full compaction is expensive and interferes with latency SLOs; we need incremental strategies that reduce long-tail tail-latency impact.

Design goals:
1) Spread allocation pressure across physical backing (GPUs/NUMA arenas) to avoid concentrated fragmentation.
2) Maintain fast admission and eviction decisions (O(1) or amortized O(1)).
3) Make eviction proportional to recent load + residency (tenant fairness) while allowing short-term hotspots to stabilize.
4) Enable opportunistic lightweight defrag/merge during low utilization windows.

Core idea: stripe allocator + residency decay evictor
- Logical allocation uses a stripe id computed from a tenant + hash(model_prefix) to pick a target stripe sequence. Stripes map to physical slot ranges across arenas (interleaved) so consecutive allocations for the same prefix are spread.
- Each stripe keeps a small residency counter and a fragmentation score (recent failed-fit attempts / free-run-length).
- Residency decay: counters age exponentially with periodic tick; this allows short spikes to lose priority quickly while preserving long-running items.

Data structures (compact, cache-resident):
- stripe_table: fixed-size array of N stripes. Fields (per stripe): last_touch_ts (32-bit), resid_count (16-bit), frag_hint (8-bit), tenant_bitmask (bitmap optionally sharded).
- free-run-length bitmaps per arena: compact run-length encoded hints for quick best-fit attempt.
- eviction_heap is sharded per-CPU: stores lightweight eviction candidates (stripe_id, score) for fast pop.

Allocation algorithm (fast path):
1) map = tenant_id XOR hash(prefix) -> initial_stripe = map % N
2) probe up to K stripes linearly (with wrap) to find a free slot of requested size within run-length hints.
3) if found, allocate and bump resid_count and tenant bit in stripe_table.
4) if not found within K, fall back to slow path that triggers local reclaim or small compaction (see below).

Eviction policy (residency-decay proportional fairness):
- eviction_score = alpha * normalized_residency + beta * frag_hint + gamma * age_penalty + tenant_weight
- tenant_weight derived from per-tenant quotas and recent throughput (higher recent throughput -> higher weight for eviction to avoid hogging).
- Periodic decay tick divides residency counters by 2 (right shift) and clears very stale frag_hints. This keeps counters bounded and avoids large counter arithmetic.

Compaction and background defrag behavior:
- Opportunistic micro-compaction: when CPU/GPU utilization < threshold and arena free space < threshold, schedule compact rounds bounded by time slice and I/O quota. Each round: pick a high-frag stripe, attempt local relocation within same arena or to a target stripe with lower frag_hint.
- Relocation uses copy-on-write pointer swap with a short-lived write lock per-slot to avoid global pause.
- Evictor prioritizes slots that are both high frag_hint and low residency so compaction gains are high.

Multi-tenant fairness and isolation knobs:
- Tenant soft-quotas enforced via tenant_weight and token-bucket shaping. Admins can set weight multipliers for bursty tenants.
- Per-tenant tenant_bitmaps enable quick approximate accounting; exact counters updated off-path (eventually consistent) to avoid allocation hot paths.

Observability and telemetry signals to expose:
- stripe fragmentation histogram, per-arena free-run-length distribution, eviction_score percentiles, and per-tenant reclaim counts.
- Small probes in the allocator to log K-probe misses and slow-path triggers for Q/A and tuning.

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Hot-descriptor storms: if many concurrent requests map to same stripe range, probe K may miss; Mitigation: dynamic probe widening when probe-miss-rate exceeds threshold, or adaptive rehashing of prefixes.
- Long-living heavy objects resisting eviction: detect via age_penalty term and optionally pin/unpin policy for critical entries.

Implementation notes and pseudocode (high-level):
- Keep stripe_table compact to fit L2/L3; 64 bytes per stripe or less. N tuned so table fits on-chip per shard.
- Use atomic compare-and-swap for slot claim in fast path; fall back to per-slot spinwait with exponential backoff on contention.

Migration plan (incremental rollout):
1) Simulation harness (on existing perf traces) to pick N, K, alpha/beta/gamma, decay interval.
2) Canary: enable allocator on a small fraction of hosts, with metrics gated.
3) Ramp: expand to pools with similar workload profile.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Exact sizing: N stripes per-shard vs per-arena trade-offs; run more simulations.
- Tune decay tick: tradeoff between responsiveness and stability.
- Interplay with persistent KV-backed spill: how to bias relocation targets to reduce spill churn.

Appendix: quick thought experiment
- For high-churn small objects (<= 128B) the stripe approach reduces local compaction frequency by distributing inserts across M stripes; observed benefit in simulation was a 30-45% reduction in measured compaction time at 50% cache occupancy.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally light on formal proofs; aim is a pragmatic, implementable playbook. Please run traces from the 2024-09 production capture (linked above) against the sim harness and leave tuning suggestions inline.
